channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes 'Semey' Special Economic Zone in Abay Region
item.description: Kazakhstan is establishing the 'Semey' Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in the Abay region to boost investment and diversify the economy. The 600-hectare zone in the Zhanasemey district will host high-tech, export-oriented enterprises. The project, aligned with presidential directives, anticipates 1.4 trillion tenge in investments and the creation of around 14,000 jobs, contributing to regional economic growth.

item.title: UN Warns of Worsening Humanitarian Crisis in Afghanistan
item.description: Afghanistan faces a worsening humanitarian crisis, with needs expected to rise sharply in 2027 due to returnees, regional instability, and El Niño, according to the UN Deputy Special Representative Bruno Lemarquis. Humanitarian funding has dropped significantly, and healthcare centers are closing. The UN urges the international community not to abandon Afghanistan.

item.title: US, China, and Russia Accelerate Hypersonic Weapons Competition
item.description: The US Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract for a new air-launched hypersonic missile, signaling an intensifying arms race with China and Russia. Hypersonic weapons, exceeding Mach 5, are difficult to track and intercept due to their speed and maneuverability.

item.title: 28 Children in Kyrgyzstan to Receive Free Cochlear Implant Surgeries from Qatari Specialists
item.description: Twenty-eight children in Kyrgyzstan with severe hearing impairments will undergo free cochlear implant surgeries performed by specialists from Qatar. The procedures will take place at the National Center for Maternity and Childhood Protection. Thirty-six children were initially selected for the program.

item.title: Pakistan's Bank Alfalah Completes Exit from Afghanistan After 20 Years, Transfers Business to Ghaznfar Bank
item.description: Pakistan-based Bank Alfalah has concluded its 20-year operations in Afghanistan, transferring its local banking business to Ghaznfar Bank. The transaction, finalized on November 5 after regulatory approvals, means Bank Alfalah has ceased its operations in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Welcomes Tajik Leader Rahmon to Astana
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev officially welcomed Tajik President Emomali Rahmon to Astana. The ceremony included a fly-past of defense force helicopters and a guard of honor. The leaders are set to discuss bilateral cooperation and strengthening their strategic partnership.

item.title: Afghan Spy Chief: Daesh Uses Telegram and TikTok for Communication and Funding
item.description: Afghanistan's intelligence chief, Abdul Haq Wasiq, stated that Daesh utilizes Telegram and TikTok for communication, financial resources, and ideological promotion. He noted that technology companies do not cooperate with Afghanistan in countering Daesh, allowing the group greater operational freedom globally. Wasiq made these remarks at the SCO Plus Expert Dialogue on Security Issues in Samarkand.

item.title: Iran Distributes Iodine Tablets Amidst Threat of US Nuclear Strike
item.description: Iran has begun distributing iodine tablets due to the threat of a potential US nuclear strike on the underground facility Pickaxe Mountain, located near the Natanz nuclear complex. Local residents are receiving iodine pills and instructions for radioactive threat scenarios. A representative from Iran's Ministry of Health confirmed the distribution, citing distrust in President Trump.

item.title: Convict Found Dead in Pavlodar Colony, Suspected Suicide
item.description: A convict serving time for a crime against a minor was found dead in a Pavlodar correctional facility. Preliminary findings suggest the individual committed suicide by hanging. Authorities have opened a criminal case and are investigating the incident, reviewing surveillance footage.

item.title: Turkey Detains Over 33,000 Afghan Migrants in First 10 Months of 2026
item.description: Turkish authorities apprehended 33,341 Afghan nationals in the first ten months of 2026, making them the largest group of undocumented migrants detained. Overall, over 120,000 foreign nationals were detained across Turkey during this period. Afghans were followed by Syrians and Uzbeks.

item.title: Over 138,000 Vials of Illegal Medicines Destroyed in Namangan
item.description: More than 138,000 vials of illegally produced medicines, along with raw materials and equipment, were destroyed in Namangan, Uzbekistan. The total value of the confiscated items is estimated at around 560 million soums. The destruction was carried out following a court decision.

item.title: Uzbek Metallurgical Plant Fined Over 1.6 Billion Sums for Environmental Damage
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change has fined the Uzmetkombinat plant 1.63 billion sums for significant environmental violations. Inspections revealed excessive atmospheric emissions, including sulfur oxide levels 1533 times above permitted limits. The plant also failed to install necessary monitoring systems.

item.title: Kant Receives 8.13 Billion Som Investment for Industrial Development and Infrastructure
item.description: Over 2021-2026, Kant, Kyrgyzstan, has attracted 8.13 billion som in investments for three major enterprises, creating 944 jobs. Investments were directed to the Kant Cement Plant (5.25 billion som), 'Stilex' (1.92 billion som), and 'BekemBlok' (962 million som). The city also saw infrastructure improvements, including school repairs and park renovations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Resolution of Contested Land Disputes Within One Year
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed officials to review and resolve contested land disputes in the Sokuluk district within one year. The directive came during a meeting with residents, one of whom raised concerns about land documentation issues. The mayor of Bishkek noted that some cases involve criminal proceedings and fraudulent sales.

item.title: Almaty Investigates Death of 14-Year-Old After Antibiotic Injection
item.description: Police in Almaty have opened a criminal case following the death of a 14-year-old boy whose condition rapidly deteriorated after receiving an antibiotic injection at a local polyclinic. The boy's mother reported that he experienced a severe reaction and lost consciousness immediately after the injection. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan secures first Olympic license for the 2028 Games
item.description: Kazakhstan has obtained its first Olympic license for the 2028 Olympic Games. This marks a significant achievement for the country's athletes as they prepare for the upcoming international competition.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Official Marriage Registration, Discourages Cohabitation
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan has called on women to officially register their marriages, emphasizing the legal protections it provides. Responding to a woman who faced property and alimony disputes after living in a civil union without registration, Japarov stated that legal recourse is impossible in such cases. He urged citizens to abandon the practice of unregistered cohabitation.

item.title: US Offers $20 Million Reward for Information on Iran's Nuclear Program
item.description: The US State Department's Rewards for Justice program is offering up to $20 million and potential relocation for information regarding Iran's nuclear program. This includes details on facilities, equipment, personnel, and movements. The US has long expressed concerns about Iran's nuclear activities and alleged pursuit of weapons.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Gas and Gasoline Imports Surge in First Nine Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $65.4 billion in January-September, a 6.3% increase year-on-year. Exports were $25.8 billion (down 5.5%), while imports hit $39.6 billion (up 15.7%). Notably, gas and gasoline imports saw a significant rise. China remains the top trading partner.

item.title: Iran Claims to Have Intercepted and Destroyed US Drone Over Southern Region
item.description: Iran's military claims it intercepted and destroyed a US MQ-9 drone over its southern region, specifically near Qeshm Island. State media reported the drone was downed by newly deployed air defense systems. This follows previous claims by the IRGC of intercepting US drones over southern Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Qatar Denies Reports of Failed US-Iran Agreement on Nuclear Deal Negotiations
item.description: Qatar's government has refuted claims that the United States and Iran have failed to reach an agreement. The Qatari International Media Office stated that reports circulating on social media were false. Qatar remains committed to coordinating with both nations to support ongoing negotiations.

item.title: US Sanctions Eight Canadian Financial Firms for Allegedly Aiding Iran Sanctions Evasion
item.description: The United States has imposed sanctions on eight Canadian financial services companies accused of facilitating Iran's evasion of US sanctions. The Treasury Department stated these firms helped Iran bypass restrictions by handling transactions involving Iranian rials and digital assets with blacklisted entities.

item.title: Man Arrested in Uzbekistan for Large-Scale Fraud Involving Loan Pledges
item.description: Authorities in the Tashkent region have arrested Pavel Kim for allegedly engaging in large-scale fraud. Kim reportedly lent money to individuals and then made them sign promissory notes for ten times the loan amount. He then used these notes to obtain court decisions in his favor, seizing victims' assets. Over 65 victims have come forward.

item.title: Qatar Continues US-Iran Negotiations Amidst Reports of New Strikes
item.description: Qatar has denied reports of stalled negotiations between the United States and Iran, stating that both sides are continuing to work towards a ceasefire agreement. This comes after the US announced new strikes on Iran's air defense systems. Qatari officials emphasized progress and the ongoing commitment to finding a resolution.

item.title: Aktobe authorities revoke permit for protest on disability rights
item.description: Aktobe city authorities have revoked a permit for a protest concerning the social rights of citizens with disabilities. The permit, initially granted for December 3rd, was cancelled due to ongoing emergency repair work by 'Aqtobe Su-Energy Group' at the designated protest site. The authorities stated that holding the peaceful assembly at the specified location and time was not possible.

item.title: China expresses serious concern to US over new trade restrictions
item.description: China has conveyed serious concern to the United States regarding recent trade and economic restrictions. The statement was made in Beijing following virtual talks on November 6th. Both sides agreed to continue trade and economic consultations to resolve disagreements through dialogue and maintain stable bilateral relations.

item.title: Canary Islands face record surge in illegal migrant arrivals
item.description: The Canary Islands are experiencing a record influx of illegal migrants, with over 3,000 arriving in the first week of November. Regional authorities deem the situation unsustainable, citing potential strain on healthcare and transport systems. At least nine migrants died during attempts to reach the islands.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces stricter penalties for fire safety violations causing harm
item.description: A new law in Uzbekistan enhances fire safety regulations and accountability. It introduces compensation for damages to life and health resulting from fire safety rule breaches. Violators may face compensation up to 3,000 base calculation units (approx. $1.3 billion) for fatalities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan sees personnel changes: dismissals at Nesk, new mayor for Karabalta
item.description: Kyrgyzstan experienced several personnel changes this week. The CEO of 'National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan' (Nesk) was dismissed, along with a deputy director. Asylbek Jenisbek was appointed the new mayor of Karabalta. Other appointments include a deputy director for the State Agency for Physical Culture and Sports.

item.title: Tajikistan Arrests Nine Suspects in International Drug Trafficking Ring
item.description: Nine individuals have been arrested in Tajikistan on suspicion of international drug trafficking. Authorities seized 24 kg of hashish, believed to have been smuggled from Afghanistan for onward transit. The alleged group leader, 44-year-old Muzaffar Azamov, is among those detained. The group is suspected of conducting 20-25 shipments totaling 550-600 kg since 2025.

item.title: Almaty: 14-Year-Old Dies After Receiving Antibiotic Injection
item.description: An investigation has begun into the death of a 14-year-old boy in Almaty, Kazakhstan, after he received an antibiotic injection. His parents report his condition rapidly deteriorated following the intramuscular administration. Doctors fought for his life for seven days. The family demands a thorough and fair investigation into the cause of death.

item.title: Tajik President Calls for Cooperation on AI Security
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon proposed integrating the Aqaba Process and Dushanbe Process to counter new threats from artificial intelligence. He highlighted AI's potential for economic and governmental advancement but warned of risks, particularly its use by terrorists for propaganda and weapon creation. Tajikistan advocates for responsible AI use.

item.title: UN Official Urges Action for Girls' Education in Afghanistan Amidst Crisis
item.description: A UN Under-Secretary-General has called for urgent action to support girls' education in Afghanistan, stating that over half of primary school-age children are out of formal education. 2.6 million girls are barred from attending school beyond Grade 6, risking an entire generation being left behind.

item.title: Daughter of detained activist Marat Turymbetov reports threat to his life
item.description: The daughter of activist Marat Turymbetov, detained in Almaty, has released a video appeal expressing concern for his life. Turymbetov, suffering from a serious kidney condition, has reportedly refused hemodialysis in protest of his detention conditions. His daughter states his life is at risk due to his illness and inadequate medical care.

item.title: Russian man arrested for disturbing flight to Tashkent sentenced to 7 days
item.description: A Russian citizen was sentenced to 7 days of administrative arrest for causing a disturbance on a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Tashkent. The man, identified as V.K., was drunk, shouted, insulted passengers and crew, and refused to comply with law enforcement demands upon arrival. He admitted guilt, expressing regret for his actions.

item.title: Turkmenistan Women Face New Hurdles Obtaining Driving Licenses
item.description: Women in Turkmenistan are reportedly facing increased difficulties in obtaining driving licenses. In some regions, women must be 50 years old to qualify. Some women who completed driving school were denied exams, with officials citing the age requirement. Bribes are allegedly being solicited.

item.title: Pakistan Reviews U.S. Proposal to Relocate Afghans via its Territory
item.description: Pakistan's Foreign Ministry confirmed it is reviewing a U.S. proposal to transfer Afghan nationals from the U.S. to Afghanistan through Pakistan. This comes after a U.S. federal court halted the plan to relocate over 150 Afghan refugees. The Taliban expressed serious concerns about third countries brokering deals.

item.title: Central Bank: Successful ATM Transaction Not Proof if Cash Not Dispensed
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank reminded commercial banks that a 'successful' ATM transaction record is insufficient proof if cash is not dispensed to the customer. The regulator stated that consumer property rights must be restored if an ATM malfunction prevents proper transaction completion.

item.title: UN: Afghanistan Imports 80% of Electricity Despite Solar Potential
item.description: The UN Development Programme (UNDP) states Afghanistan imports 80% of its electricity needs, spending over $280 million annually, despite vast solar energy potential. The 'Afghanistan Energy Week' event aims to foster cooperation and reduce reliance on energy imports.

item.title: Kazakhstan President's Address on National Development Discussed by Experts
item.description: Experts gathered at the Presidential Center to discuss the President's Address to the People of Kazakhstan. They evaluated pressing issues of state development, proposed approaches, and ways to implement set priorities. The address outlines a comprehensive modernization of the country across economic, social, and political spheres.
